newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian security chief ends teachers strike.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian security chief ends teachers strike.

text.p: West Bank teachers agreed on Wednesday to end their strike, the first by Palestinian government employees, after talks with a PLO security chief, teachers said.
Palestinian police arrested in the West Bank on Monday more than 25 teachers who were leading the strike in thousands of public schools for higher salaries and improved conditions.

About 70 percent of the 18,000 striking teachers returned to their classes in public schools in the West Bank towns of Hebron, Nablus and Jenin on Wednesday but classrooms remained shut in Ramallah, teachers said.
In a bid to persuade the holdouts to go back to work, Jibril Rajoub, head of the Palestinian Preventive Security agency, met in Ramallah with the detained strike committee.
After the meeting, both sides issued a statement saying: "The strike will end as of Thursday morning."
The detained teachers were released, witnesses said.
Abdelnasser Ahmad Ali, a teacher from Ramallah, said the strike leaders had bowed to pressure from the self-rule administration to go back to work.

Another Ramallah teacher, who would only give her first name, Sana, told Reuters: "The security apparatus of the Palestinian Authority, led by Rajoub, brought the coordination committee from prison and pressured them to end the strike.
"They closed the door and prevented them from leaving without signing," she said.
Jibril made no comment to reporters as he left the meeting. But he said earlier: "We have partially accepted the (teachers') demands."
The strike, which began at the start of April, was the first labour dispute involving Palestinian Authority employees.
Teachers have complained they receive about $400 a month, a sum which they say is not enough to cover their basic needs.
